([[Arlington County, Virginia]]) | college = *[[Southern Miss Golden Eagles basketball|Southern Miss]] (2014–2016) *[[Montana State Bobcats men's basketball|Montana State]] (2017–2019) | draft_year = 2019 | career_start = 2019 | years1 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2019–2020]] | team1 = [[Northern Arizona Suns]] | years2 = {{nbay|2020|start}}–{{nbay|2021|end}} | team2 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years3 = [[2022–23 Liga Națională (men's basketball)|2022–2023]] | team3 = [[CS Rapid București (men's basketball)|Rapid București]] | years4 = 2023–2024 | team4 = [[Sudbury Five]] | years5 = 2024 | team5 = [[Pacific Caesar]] | years6 = 2024–present | team6 = [[Bima Perkasa Jogja]] | highlights = }} '''Keljin DeShawn Blevins''' (born November 24, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Bima Perkasa Jogja]] of the [[Indonesian Basketball League]] (IBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles basketball|Southern Miss Golden Eagles]] and [[Montana State Bobcats men's basketball|Montana State Bobcats]]. ==Early life and high school== Blevins was born and grew up in [[Hot Springs, Arkansas]] and initially attended [[Lakeside High School (Hot Springs, Arkansas)|Lakeside High School]]. He averaged 10 points and 7.3 rebounds per game and helped lead the Rams to a 5A-South conference title as a junior. Blevins transferred to [[Bishop O'Connell High School]] in [[Arlington County, Virginia]] for his senior year and was named honorable mention All-[[Washington Catholic Athletic Conference]]. ==College career== Blevins began his collegiate career at [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles basketball|Southern Mississippi]]. He averaged 1.8 points and 1.8 rebounds in 25 games in his freshman season. As a sophomore, Blevins averaged 5.8 points and 3.4 rebounds in 22.3 minutes over 29 games, 24 of which he started.{{cite web|url=https://skylinesportsmt.com/southern-miss-transfer-blevins-officially-a-bobcat/|title=Southern Miss transfer Blevins officially a Bobcat|first=Colter|last=Nuanez|website=skylinesportsmt.com|date=August 17, 2016|access-date=November 26, 2020}} After the season, he decided to transfer to [[Montana State University]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bozemandailychronicle.com/blogs/bobcats/mens_basketball/southern-mississippi-guard-blevins-transferring-to-montana-state/article_00b8fd5d-6a2d-5787-926f-7b2185fba63a.html|title=Southern Mississippi guard Blevins transferring to Montana State|first=Parker|last=Gabriel|work=[[Bozeman Daily Chronicle]]|date=August 14, 2016|access-date=November 26, 2020}} After sitting out one year due to NCAA transfer rules, Blevins entered his [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] junior season as a starter for the [[Montana State Bobcats men's basketball|Bobcats]] and averaged 9.7 points and 5.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.hotsr.com/news/2018/nov/29/big-sky-is-no-limit-blevins-looks-to-fi/|title=Big Sky is no limit: Blevins looks to finish college career on high note|work=[[Hot Springs Sentinel-Record]]|date=November 29, 2018|access-date=November 26, 2020}} In the final game of his college career on March 14, 2019, Blevins scored a career-high 27 points in a 90–84 loss to [[2018–19 Eastern Washington Eagles men's basketball team|Eastern Washington]].{{cite news |title=Peatling lifts EWU to 90–84 win in Big Sky quarterfinal |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401121779 |access-date=November 28, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 15, 2019}} As a redshirt senior, he averaged 11.8 points and a team-high 5.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://helenair.com/sports/college/big-sky-conference/montana-state-university/former-montana-state-forward-keljin-blevins-signs-with-portland-trail-blazers/article_3fb63527-cc31-5a90-adb7-b94bcf6f8929.html|title=Former Blevins was selected with the 15th overall pick in the 2019 NBA G League Draft by the [[Northern Arizona Suns]].{{cite web |last=Morgan |first=Madison |date=October 26, 2019 |title=MSU Billings Basketball alumni drafted to the NBA G-League |url=https://www.ktvq.com/sports/msu-billings-basketball-alumni-drafted-to-the-nba-g-league |access-date=November 26, 2020 |website=[[KTVQ|KTVQ.com]]}} He averaged 4.3 points and 2.8 rebounds in 35 games in his first professional season.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/trail-blazers/damian-lillards-cousin-keljin-blevins-signs-two-way-contract-trail-blazers|title=Damian Lillard's cousin Keljin Blevins signs two-way contract with Trail Blazers|first=Jonathan|last=Warner|website=[[NBC Sports Northwest]]|date=November 25, 2020|access-date=November 26, 2020|archive-date=January 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210120144535/https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/trail-blazers/damian-lillards-cousin-keljin-blevins-signs-two-way-contract-trail-blazers|url-status=dead}} Blevins made his NBA debut on December 23, 2020, playing four minutes while shooting 0-for-2 from the field with one assist in the fourth quarter of a 100–120 loss to the [[2020–21 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]] in the Blazers' season opener. The appearance made him the first former Montana State player to play in an NBA game.{{cite web|url=https://www.bozemandailychronicle.com/sports/bobcats/mens-basketball/keljin-blevins-becomes-first-former-bobcat-to-play-in-nba-regular-season-game/article_f08ea641-6422-592c-9c23-e737b9084589.html|title=Keljin Blevins becomes first former Bobcat to play in NBA regular season game|work=[[Bozeman Daily Chronicle]]|date=December 24, 2020|access-date=December 24, 2020}} On September 23, 2021, Blevins signed another two-way contract with the Trail Blazers.{{cite web |date=September 23, 2021 |title=Trail Blazers announce Training Camp roster |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-announce-training-camp-roster-0 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924000622/https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-announce-training-camp-roster-0 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 24, 2021 |access-date=September 23, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} ===Rapid București (2022–2023)=== In 2022, Blevins joined [[CS Rapid București (men's basketball)|Rapid București]] of the [[Liga Națională (men's basketball)|Liga Națională]], averaging 4.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game. He was released on March 3, 2023.{{cite web |last=Beres |first=Arnold |title=Rapid cut Blevins |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Romania/news/796428/Rapid-cut-Blevins |website=Eurobasket
